name: Miles Brewton House

dates.note: The SC register says 'ca. 1765-1769'; the 1930s survey sheet says 'built by Miles Brewton about 1765' (OCR 'l 7b5'); the Wikipedia infobox prints 1765 and its text 'c. 1765–1769'; the node's exemplar says 1769 and names Ezra Waite. Recorded as the state register states it.

quotes.text: Historical Data: HABS No. SC-78 Page 1 HA.BS SC, 10-CHAR, 5-The fine house built by Miles :Brewton about l 7b5 is known today as the Pringle House on King Street. It is a square 11double house", has fine iron fence, double gateway, portico very handsome, two tiers of stone pillars are im-pressive. ~aneling, ceilings, cornices, mantel-pieces and other details are noticeably fine examples of their period.
quotes.page: HABS No. SC-78 Page 1 -- the marker falls inside the span, as quoted

quotes.text: It was doubted by some that Ezra Waite did the architecture and conducted the execution thereof. Therefore, Mr. Waite made a public announcement to the effect that he did the work and offered "One Hundred Guineas" to anyone who could prove to the contrary. It was never known whether the 110ne Hundred Guineas 11 were ever claimed .• The Gardens originally extended through to Legare Street. Mr. Brewton did not long enjoy his new home for he, his wife and children were all lost at sea in 1775 on their way to Philadelphia and the property passed to his sisters, Mrs. Pinckney and Mrs. Motte. After the capture of Charleston, this house was used as the :British headquarters and occupied by Sir Henry Clinton,
